scope: Trauma neurobiology, attachment and autonomic claims, ASD/psychiatric qEEG language, large-scale network claims, EMDR mechanisms, dissociation, developmental trauma, personality neuroscience, moral injury and psychiatric-state confounds.
governanceFindings: Specific neuroscience claims were strengthened with claim-relevant reviews, meta-analyses, guidelines or theory-specific sources.
Group-level neuroimaging, EEG, autonomic and endocrine findings were not treated as individual diagnostic biomarkers.
Attachment classifications were not treated as fixed neural types.
Window of Tolerance and structural dissociation were retained as clinical or theoretical models rather than validated anatomical states.
EMDR clinical efficacy was kept distinct from unresolved or partially supported mechanism theories.
Fear extinction, prediction error and memory mechanisms were framed as probabilistic learning constructs rather than universal explanations of PTSD.
Moral injury was distinguished from PTSD and from a discrete neurobiological disorder.
No BPD-specific neuroscience evidence was generalised to personality disorders as a whole.
boundary: This is an internal evidence-governance review. It does not constitute independent external clinician peer review and does not satisfy the release-manifest externalReview.clinical requirement for a public v1.0 claim.
nextPriority: Prepare external clinical reviewer pack and sign-off checklist, then resolve remaining accessibility and legal/licensing pre-v1.0 governance gates.

concepts.note: Added current trauma-neurobiology review. Existing acute stress content remains appropriately contextual and does not imply that normal acute threat responses inevitably progress to PTSD.
Added current AIP-specific and state-of-science reviews. AIP is retained as an EMDR theoretical framework, not presented as a proven literal neural-storage mechanism.
Added current PTSD neurobiology and emotional-processing meta-analysis. Affect-regulation mechanisms remain group-level and heterogeneous rather than diagnostic neural signatures.
Added current stress-neurobiology review. Amygdala findings remain framed as heterogeneous group-level associations rather than a universal overactive-amygdala rule.
Added attachment-specific systematic review. Existing non-deterministic language retained; attachment representations are not treated as fixed neural types.
Current autonomic anatomy and physiology reviewed. Existing content is appropriately contextual and non-diagnostic; only the evidence base was refreshed.
Reviewed bilateral stimulation against current EMDR evidence. Working-memory effects have empirical support, but bilateral stimulation is not presented as having one settled or complete mechanism.
Added PTSD-specific neuroimaging meta-analysis supporting network-level involvement while preserving state, comorbidity and diagnostic-specificity caveats.
Added current review of stress-related brain morphology. Chronic stress effects remain described as plastic and heterogeneous rather than inevitable damage.

Reviewed clinical indication claims against current systematic-review and PTSD guideline evidence. PTSD indication remains supported; broader applications should not inherit the same evidence strength automatically.
Reviewed clinical-integration and limitation content. Existing distinction between treatment evidence, clinical judgement and unresolved mechanisms remains appropriate.
Added CPTSD-specific neurobiological review. Existing statement that no validated biomarker distinguishes CPTSD clinically was retained.

Reviewed precautions against current PTSD guidance and EMDR state-of-science literature. Individual assessment, stabilisation needs, comorbidity and capacity to engage remain clinical considerations rather than universal absolute contraindications.
Added PTSD resting-state systematic review/meta-analysis. Existing group-level, non-diagnostic network language retained.
Reviewed general DMN content. Existing foundational and review sources remain appropriate; record does not treat DMN variation as a psychiatric diagnosis or private-thought readout.
Added systematic review of childhood adversity and neural development. Existing non-deterministic developmental framing retained.
Added dissociation-specific functional neuroimaging systematic review. Existing heterogeneous and non-diagnostic framing retained.

Reviewed the structured EMDR treatment framework. Procedural description remains appropriate and is kept distinct from claims that every phase has an independently established neurobiological mechanism.

Reviewed emotion-regulation network content. Existing cognitive-control and emotion-regulation sources remain suitable for general mechanisms; no single neural circuit is presented as a diagnostic marker.
Added current PTSD neurobiology and psychotherapy neuroimaging synthesis. Existing mechanistic language remains bounded because treatment-related activation findings are tentative and heterogeneous.
Added current translational meta-analysis and robustness analysis. Fear-learning abnormalities are retained as group-level mechanisms, not universal individual deficits.
Added current meta-analytic and multiverse evidence. Record should not imply that impaired extinction retention is universal in PTSD because findings vary by paradigm and analysis.
Added current comprehensive PTSD neurobiology review. Foundational content remains explicitly heterogeneous and avoids single-region or single-mechanism explanations.
Reviewed frontoparietal control-network content. Existing sources appropriately support general network function and individual variability without diagnostic overreach.
Reviewed foundational network-neuroscience content. Existing Yeo and Bassett/Sporns sources remain appropriate for general functional-network principles; no disorder-specific inference is required.
Added current stress-neurobiology review. Existing non-deterministic interpretation retained; hippocampal structural findings are not individual diagnostic markers.
Added PTSD-specific HPA-axis meta-analysis. Existing cautious wording retained because direction and magnitude of endocrine findings vary across methods and samples.

Reviewed competing EMDR mechanism accounts. Working-memory, memory-updating/reconsolidation and AIP explanations remain plausible or partially supported components rather than one established complete causal mechanism.

Added current PTSD neurobiology synthesis. Consolidation is retained as a normal memory process relevant to trauma, without implying that traumatic memories are stored through a unique pathological consolidation mechanism.
Added current PTSD neurobiology synthesis. Trauma-related encoding effects remain contextual and probabilistic rather than evidence of a distinct or universally fragmented traumatic-memory system.

Added moral-injury-specific reviews. Moral injury is distinguished from PTSD and framed as a multidimensional psychological, social, ethical and potentially spiritual construct rather than a discrete neural disorder.
Reviewed neurobiological mechanism language. Clinical efficacy does not establish a unique neural mechanism, and neuroimaging findings remain group-level and mechanistically non-specific.
Reviewed the orienting-response account as one proposed EMDR mechanism. It is not presented as the established or exclusive explanation for treatment effects.
Added current physiological review clarifying RSA/HRV measurement limits. Existing caution that HRV is not a direct measure of psychological safety retained.

Reviewed against current personality-neuroscience literature. Dimensional, heterogeneous, non-localising and non-diagnostic framing remains appropriate. Disorder-specific BPD evidence was not generalised to personality disorders as a whole.

Reviewed prediction-error claims against current fear-learning evidence. Prediction error remains a useful learning construct, not a single established causal mechanism explaining PTSD or trauma recovery.
Added current stress-neurobiology review. Existing network and state-dependent framing retained rather than reducing trauma to prefrontal underactivity.

Added current systematic review of depression-related cognitive effects. Mood, motivation, sleep, medication and other state factors remain important interpretive variables and should not automatically be reified as fixed neurological impairment.
Added current depression-specific meta-analysis supporting cautious interpretation of frontal alpha asymmetry and non-diagnostic use.
Added autism-specific systematic review and meta-analysis supporting heterogeneous group-level EEG findings and non-diagnostic individual use.
Added PTSD-specific neuroimaging meta-analysis. Existing non-diagnostic group-level framing retained.
Reviewed general salience-network content. Existing foundational and triple-network sources remain appropriate when interpreted as network models rather than disorder-specific biomarkers.
Added theory-specific foundational source. Record continues to identify structural dissociation as a theoretical clinical model rather than an anatomical partition or established neural mechanism.
Added trauma-specific autonomic meta-analysis. Existing caution that sympathetic activation is context-dependent and not equivalent to fear or diagnosis was retained.
Added theory-specific source and explicitly bounded the Window of Tolerance as a clinical heuristic/model rather than a validated measurable neurobiological threshold.
